decisions.context: Weekly forecasts depend on recurring historical sales and product/store records. The brief does not specify source systems, so choose an ingestion pattern suited to periodic data.
decisions.rationale: A batch extraction and transformation path aligns with weekly forecasting and avoids introducing streaming operations absent a freshness requirement. The design point check reports no warnings for this choice; the combination is unattested.
consequences: Source snapshots and transformations need versioning.

decisions.context: Weekly preparation, training, evaluation, and scoring must repeat reliably, while model ideas should move through the same controlled path. Manual execution would leave recurring steps dependent on team members.
decisions.rationale: An orchestrated pipeline makes the recurring weekly run repeatable and gives new candidates a consistent route through evaluation. Sources “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline” and “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” support this approach; the checked point has no warnings, though the combination is unattested.
consequences: Failed stages require clear retry and recovery behavior.

decisions.context: Reproducing a forecast for any past week requires identifying the data, code, dependencies, configuration, and model used at that time. New model candidates also need comparable experiment records.
decisions.rationale: The brief’s historical replay requirement calls for a complete record, not only a saved model file. “MLOps: What It Is, Why it Matters, and How To Implement It” and Microsoft’s “MLOps: Model management, deployment, and monitoring” describe governance spanning runs, datasets, artifacts, and deployment state. The checked point has no warnings but is unattested.
consequences: Retain immutable input snapshots or equivalent recoverable data versions.
Record code, dependencies, parameters, and model artifacts for each run.

decisions.context: New forecasting ideas must reach production quickly without disrupting the weekly run. Candidate models need a repeatable pre-promotion quality check.
decisions.rationale: Offline checks let candidates be assessed before the production weekly run, which best addresses safe iteration. “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” and “MLOps Principles” describe evaluation as part of the production pipeline; the checked point has no warnings but is unattested.
consequences: Define forecast metrics and promotion thresholds.
Keep evaluation data separate from training and tuning.

decisions.context: Model and pipeline changes need a controlled path to production without endangering the recurring forecast. Staged automation can apply checks before promotion.
decisions.rationale: Commit-triggered builds and staged promotion fit the desire to deliver ideas quickly while applying checks before production. “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” and “Continuous Intelligence: Moving Machine Learning Application into Production Reliably” support this pattern. The checked point has no warnings but is unattested.
consequences: Maintain separate validation and production stages.
A failed gate blocks promotion until resolved.

decisions.context: The product requires a forecast once per week for each store and product, with no online request or low-latency requirement stated. A scheduled scoring job can publish a complete forecast set.
decisions.rationale: Scheduled batch scoring directly fits weekly demand forecasts and avoids operating a request-serving path not required by the brief. “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline” and “Three Levels of ML Software” discuss scheduled batch prediction; the checked point has no warnings but is unattested.
consequences: Publish forecasts as a versioned weekly output.
Define behavior for incomplete or failed scoring runs.

decisions.context: A past forecast can only be reproduced if the historical inputs and their transformation history remain available. Preserving provenance is therefore part of the replay capability.
decisions.rationale: Immutable, traceable source data supports reconstructing inputs for any historical week, directly serving the brief’s reproducibility requirement. “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline” and “Architecting a Machine Learning System for Risk” support preserving original data and provenance. The checked point has no warnings but is unattested.
consequences: Set retention rules for historical source data.
Link each forecast run to its input snapshot.

decisions.context: Three data scientists own the end-to-end pipeline, so the process should allow rapid model exploration without relying on separate specialist teams for every change.
decisions.rationale: Short iterations let the team explore model ideas while the shared pipeline and release gates protect the recurring run. “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” and “MLOps Principles” support iterative delivery; the checked point has no warnings but is unattested.
consequences: Automated pipeline checks carry part of the safety burden.

uncovered: Forecasting-specific model family and seasonal or hierarchical structure.
Time-aware validation, rolling backtests, forecast horizon, and metric selection.
Data source contracts, correction handling, and store/product key quality rules.
Weekly scheduling deadlines, missed-run recovery, and output consumer interface.
